..
A mostly dry and stable air induced by the ridge that moved in
following STY Champi's west to the west, will continue overnight
through Wednesday night. After, a trade trough coming in from the
east is expected to move in, bringing low-end patchy showers enhanced
by the subtropical ridge building across the western Pacific for a
few more days, followed by a return of another tropical ridge during
the weekend.

Marine...
Combined seas of 5 to 7 feet are expected through at least Wednesday
night, to then briefly increase a foot or two coming into the second
half of the week. This is due to a strengthening northeasterly 
swell, and a secondary westerly swell produced by distant STY Champi.
As such, moderate risk of rip currents is also expected along north,
east, and west facing reefs of the Marianas for much of this week.

Tropical Systems...
At 1 PM ChST, Super Typhoon Champi was located about 680 miles west-
northwest of Guam near 16N135E, moving west-northwest at 14 mph. 
Maximum sustained winds decreased to 150 mph. Champi is expected to 
continue moving west-northwest over the next couple of days, with
little change in forward speed. STY Champi looks to maintain this
intensity tonight, then strengthen again Tuesday.

For more information on STY Champi, see bulletins issued by the 
Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN32 PGTW and by the
National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ32 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
The detached monsoon trough over eastern Micronesia will be the main
driver for the pattern over the next several days. The monsoon flow
south of the trough is generating scattered showers and a few 
thunderstorms near Kosrae and Majuro. For Kosrae, an outflow 
boundary, seen over the southern waters, is pushing north and is 
expected to bring scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms to 
Kosrae tonight. This convection looks to slowly move west, hanging 
out in Kosrae through Wednesday night before a dry pattern returns to
the island. For Majuro, convection associated with the monsoon 
trough and with a trade-wind trough to the north is filling in to 
bring scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms to the atoll later
tonight. This convection looks to persist through Wednesday night, 
with a dry pattern moving into the atoll for the remainder of the 
week through the weekend. For Pohnpei, as the convection moves west 
out of Kosrae, showers and thunderstorms will increase over the 
island, with scattered showers expected there by Wednesday night. 
Pohnpei won't see the drier pattern until the weekend beginning
Friday. As the monsoon trough begins to re-develop farther south, 
Pohnpei could see an increase in convection again late in the 
weekend.

For the marine forecast, not much going on over the next few days.
Mostly gentle to moderate winds are expected through the weekend at
Majuro. For Kosrae and Pohnpei, mostly light to gentle winds through
the weekend, with Pohnpei seeing occasional moderate winds midweek.
Combined seas look to remain between 3 and 6 feet across the region
through the week, with Kosrae seeing a southeast swell through most
of the week, becoming east Friday. Majuro and Pohnpei can expect a
northeast to east swell through the weekend.

Western Micronesia...
The effects of Super Typhoon Champi continue to be felt across
northern Palau and Yap, as the overnight altimetry pass showed winds
of 15 to 20 knots. The daytime pass didn't sample either location
good. Satellite imagery shows both locations remain in a
convectively-active rainband associated with the southwest monsoon.
As such, we opted to keep the advisory going through 5 AM Wednesday,
after which time models show decreasing winds and rainfall, with just
isolated showers expected for the remainder of the forecast. Winds
will also become light to gentle for the latter half of the week for
both locations, with seas diminishing faster at Yap than northern 
Palau.

For Chuuk, a small/weak circulation is positioned to your southeast.
This feature will slowly drift west-northwest the next few days,
keeping scattered showers in for forecast through early next week,
with light to gentle winds and seas mainly in the 3 to 5 foot range.
